tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## 4bdddc46-3b80-45ec-bc37-523e74d4fda6
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

"""Channel motion-graphics library: brand-consistent HyperFrames templates -> cached .mov/.mp4 clips. Layout (studio/motion/): shared/mc.css, shared/mc.js shared Minecraft-flavoured primitives + helpers (canonical) fonts/ brand fonts copied from Editing Pack/Fonts templates// SOURCES: template.json (manifest), markup.html, template.css, template.js templates//landscape/ GENERATED HyperFrames project (960x540 logical canvas) templates//vertical/ GENERATED HyperFrames project (540x960 logical canvas) cache/-. rendered clips Generated projects are self-contained (HyperFrames forbids ../ asset paths and one root composition per project), so each gets a lib/ copy of shared/ + fonts and a brand.css built from studio/brand/brand.json. `build()` regenerates them; `render()` calls it automatically. Previews render the logical canvas natively at 30fps; full renders supersample x2 to 1920x1080 / 1080x1920 at 60fps. from mcstudio import motion path = motion.render("time_card", {"text": "3 HOURS LATER"}) # alpha ProRes 4444 .mov path = motion.render("title_card", {"title": "DAY 1"}, opaque=True) # opaque .mp4 card CLI (wired as `mcs motion`): list | render --var k=v ... [--vertical] [--preview] [--opaque] [--duration S] | build [names] """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import base64 import hashlib import json import os import re import shutil import subprocess import sys import tempfile import time from pathlib import Path from .paths import STUDIO MOTION = STUDIO / "motion" TEMPLATES = MOTION / "templates" SHARED = MOTION / "shared" FONTS = MOTION / "fonts" CACHE = MOTION / "cache" BUILD = MOTION / "_build" # staged copies for duration overrides BRAND_JSON = STUDIO / "brand" / "brand.json" HYPERFRAMES = os.environ.get("MCS_HYPERFRAMES", "hyperframes@0.8.137") GSAP_URL = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js" # Font files (copied from Editing Pack/Fonts into studio/motion/fonts) and their CSS families. FONT_FACES = [ ("MC Ten", "Minecraft Ten.ttf"), ("Luckiest Guy", "Luckiest Guy.ttf"), ("Minecraft", "Minecraft Regular.otf"), ("Minecraft Bold", "Minecraft Bold.otf"), ] # orientation -> (logical canvas, supersample preset for full renders) ORIENTATIONS = { "landscape": ((960, 540), "landscape"), "vertical": ((540, 960), "portrait"), } SOURCE_FILES = ("template.json", "markup.html", "template.css", "template.js") # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- brand def load_brand() -> dict: return json.loads(BRAND_JSON.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) def _manifest(name: str) -> dict: p = TEMPLATES / name / "template.json" if not p.exists(): have = ", ".join(t["name"] for t in list_templates()) raise ValueError(f"unknown motion template '{name}' (have: {have})") m = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) m["name"] = name m.setdefault("orientations", list(ORIENTATIONS)) return m def list_templates() -> list[dict]: """All templates with their manifest (name, description, duration, kind, orientations, vars...).""" out = [] if TEMPLATES.exists(): for d in sorted(TEMPLATES.iterdir()): if (d / "template.json").exists(): out.append(_manifest(d.name)) return out _HTML = """ {name} ({orientation})
{markup}
""" def _write_if_changed(p: Path, data: bytes) -> bool: if p.exists() and p.read_bytes() == data: return False p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) p.write_bytes(data) return True def _fmt_num(x: float) -> str: return str(int(x)) if float(x).is_integer() else str(x) def build(name: str) -> list[Path]: """Regenerate templates/// projects. Only touches files whose content changed.""" m = _manifest(name) tdir = TEMPLATES / name brand = load_brand() decl = [] for key, spec in m.get("vars", {}).items(): d = _brand_lookup(brand, spec["brand"]) if "brand" in spec else spec.get("default") decl.append({"id": key, "type": spec.get("type", "string"), "label": spec.get("label", key), "default": d}) decl_s = json.dumps(decl, ensure_ascii=False).replace("'", "'") markup_p = tdir / "markup.html" markup = markup_p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip() if markup_p.exists() else "" markup = "\n".join(" " + ln if ln.strip() else ln for ln in markup.splitlines()) css = brand_css(brand).encode("utf-8") out = [] for orientation in m["orientations"]: (w, h), _ = ORIENTATIONS[orientation] pdir = tdir / orientation html = _HTML.format(name=name, decl=decl_s, w=w, h=h, dur=_fmt_num(float(m["duration"])), orientation=orientation, markup=markup, gsap=GSAP_URL) _write_if_changed(pdir / "index.html", html.encode("utf-8")) for f in ("template.css", "template.js"): if (tdir / f).exists(): _write_if_changed(pdir / f, (tdir / f).read_bytes()) for f in SHARED.glob("*"): if f.is_file(): _write_if_changed(pdir / "lib" / f.name, f.read_bytes()) for _, fname in FONT_FACES: _write_if_changed(pdir / "lib" / "fonts" / fname, (FONTS / fname).read_bytes()) _write_if_changed(pdir / "lib" / "brand.css", css) out.append(pdir) return out def _coerce(spec: dict, value): t = spec.get("type", "string") if t == "number": f = float(value) return int(f) if f.is_integer() else f if t == "boolean": if isinstance(value, bool): return value return str(value).strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on") return str(value) def resolve_vars(name: str, vars: dict | None = None) -> dict: """Manifest defaults (brand refs resolved from brand.json) overlaid with caller vars, type-coerced.""" m = _manifest(name) brand = load_brand() specs = m.get("vars", {}) out = {} for key, spec in specs.items(): out[key] = _brand_lookup(brand, spec["brand"]) if "brand" in spec else spec.get("default") for key, val in (vars or {}).items(): if key not in specs: raise ValueError(f"template '{name}' has no var '{key}' (vars: {', '.join(specs)})") out[key] = val out = {k: _coerce(specs[k], v) for k, v in out.items()} for k, v in out.items(): # render page is served over http: inline local images if isinstance(v, str) and v and not v.startswith(("data:", "http:", "https:")) \ and Path(v).suffix.lower() in _IMG_MIME: f = next((c for c in (Path(v), STUDIO / v, STUDIO.parent / v) if c.is_file()), None) if f: # absolute, studio-relative or channel-relative path out[k] = f"data:{_IMG_MIME[f.suffix.lower()]};base64," + base64.b64encode(f.read_bytes()).decode() return out _IMG_MIME = {".png": "image/png", ".jpg": "image/jpeg", ".jpeg": "image/jpeg", ".gif": "image/gif", ".webp": "image/webp", ".svg": "image/svg+xml"} def _fingerprint(tdir: Path) -> list: files = [tdir / f for f in SOURCE_FILES if (tdir / f).exists()] files += [p for p in sorted(SHARED.glob("*")) if p.is_file()] files += [FONTS / f for _, f in FONT_FACES] + [BRAND_JSON] return [[p.name, p.stat().st_mtime_ns, p.stat().st_size] for p in files] def _npx() -> str: exe = shutil.which("npx") or shutil.which("npx.cmd") if not exe: raise RuntimeError("npx not found on PATH (Node 22+ is required for HyperFrames)") return exe def _stage_duration(pdir: Path, base: float, duration: float, key: str) -> Path: """Copy a built project with root/clip data-duration rewritten (HyperFrames fixes it at compile time).""" dst = BUILD / key if dst.exists(): shutil.rmtree(dst) shutil.copytree(pdir, dst) p = dst / "index.html" html = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") html = html.replace(f'data-duration="{_fmt_num(base)}"', f'data-duration="{_fmt_num(duration)}"') p.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8") return dst def render(name: str, vars: dict | None = None, orientation: str = "landscape", preview: bool = False, opaque: bool = False, duration: float | None = None, force: bool = False, verbose: bool = False) -> Path: """Render a template to studio/motion/cache/-. and return the path (cached). orientation: "landscape" (1920x1080) or "vertical" (1080x1920). preview=True -> 960x540/540x960 @30fps. opaque=True -> mp4 on the brand ink background (card segments); default ProRes 4444 .mov with alpha. duration: override length for manifests with "stretchable": true (the hold section grows). The hash covers name + resolved vars + orientation + preview + opaque + duration + source/shared/font file mtimes + brand.json, so edits to a template invalidate its cache. """ if orientation not in ORIENTATIONS: raise ValueError(f"orientation must be one of {list(ORIENTATIONS)}") m = _manifest(name) if orientation not in m["orientations"]: raise ValueError(f"template '{name}' has no {orientation} version") tdir = TEMPLATES / name _, res_preset = ORIENTATIONS[orientation] rv = resolve_vars(name, vars) if "opaque" in m.get("vars", {}): rv["opaque"] = bool(opaque) elif opaque: raise ValueError(f"template '{name}' does not support opaque renders") base_dur = float(m["duration"]) if duration is None and m.get("duration_rule") == "from + 1" and "from" in rv: duration = float(rv["from"]) + 1 # countdown: one second per number + GO! if duration is not None: duration = float(duration) if abs(duration - base_dur) < 1e-6: duration = None elif not m.get("stretchable"): raise ValueError(f"template '{name}' is not stretchable; its duration is fixed at {base_dur}s") elif duration < float(m.get("min_duration", base_dur)): raise ValueError(f"template '{name}' needs at least {m.get('min_duration', base_dur)}s") key_src = json.dumps({ "name": name, "vars": rv, "orientation": orientation, "preview": bool(preview), "opaque": bool(opaque), "duration": duration, "hf": HYPERFRAMES, "files": _fingerprint(tdir), }, sort_keys=True) h = hashlib.sha256(key_src.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12] ext = "mp4" if opaque else "mov" CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) out = CACHE / f"{name}-{h}.{ext}" if out.exists() and out.stat().st_size > 0 and not force: return out build(name) pdir = tdir / orientation proj = pdir if duration is None else _stage_duration(pdir, base_dur, duration, f"{name}-{h}") fd, var_file = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f".{name}-", suffix=".json", dir=CACHE) with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump(rv, f) tmp_out = CACHE / f".{name}-{h}.part.{ext}" cmd = [_npx(), "--yes", HYPERFRAMES, "render", str(proj), "--format", ext, "--fps", "30" if preview else "60", "--variables-file", var_file, "--strict-variables", "-o", str(tmp_out)] if not preview: cmd += ["--resolution", res_preset] if ext == "mp4": cmd += ["--quality", "draft" if preview else "high"] if not verbose: cmd.append("--quiet") t0 = time.time() try: r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=not verbose, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") if r.returncode != 0 or not tmp_out.exists() or tmp_out.stat().st_size == 0: tail = ((r.stdout or "") + "\n" + (r.stderr or ""))[-3000:] if not verbose else "" raise RuntimeError(f"hyperframes render failed for '{name}' (exit {r.returncode}):\n{tail}") os.replace(tmp_out, out) finally: for p in (Path(var_file), tmp_out): try: p.unlink() except OSError: pass if proj != pdir: shutil.rmtree(proj, ignore_errors=True) if verbose: print(f"[motion] {name} rendered in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s", file=sys.stderr) return out # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- CLI

"""Render + inspect a motion template.
usage: uv run python mt.py NAME [--vars JSON] [--o landscape,vertical] [--t 0.3,0.6] [--full] [--alpha] [--dur S]
Writes PNGs to scratchpad/out/<name>_<o>_<tag>_<t>_{gray,game}.png and prints alpha stats.
"""
import argparse, json, subprocess, sys, os
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

STUDIO = Path(r"C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Minecraft Channel\studio")
sys.path.insert(0, str(STUDIO))
os.chdir(STUDIO)
from mcstudio import motion

OUT = Path(__file__).parent / "out"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

def game_bg(w, h):
    p = OUT / f"_game_{w}x{h}.png"
    if not p.exists():
        src = OUT / "_game_src.png"
        if not src.exists():
            subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-ss", "30", "-i",
                            str(STUDIO / "projects/auto-dig/work/full/base.mkv"), "-frames:v", "1", str(src)], check=True)
        im = Image.open(src).convert("RGB")
        # cover-crop
        sw, sh = im.size
        s = max(w / sw, h / sh)
        im = im.resize((round(sw * s), round(sh * s)))
        l = (im.width - w) // 2; t = (im.height - h) // 2
        im.crop((l, t, l + w, t + h)).save(p)
    return Image.open(p).convert("RGB")

"""Browser-playable previews of the motion-graphics templates (for the studio UI's Motion graphics page).

For each template: render it in preview mode (landscape, default vars) via motion.render, composite the
alpha .mov over a Minecraft gameplay still, and write
    studio/motion/previews/<name>.mp4    h264 960x540 30fps, +0.5s tail so it loops cleanly
    studio/motion/previews/<name>.jpg    poster (mid-frame)
    studio/motion/previews/<name>.json   {"mov": "<cached .mov name>"}: the cache key
Templates are discovered from studio/motion/templates/ on every call (never a fixed list). A preview is
only rebuilt when motion.render returns a different .mov (i.e. the template, shared files or brand changed).

The gameplay still is extracted once from a project's game recording (test-clip-02 first) into
previews/_bg_<orientation>.jpg; with no recording available a dark checkerboard is generated instead.

CLI (from studio/):
    uv run python -m mcstudio.motion_previews [names...] [--missing] [--force]
    uv run python -m mcstudio.motion_previews --render NAME [--vars JSON] [--orientation O] [--preview]
        (used by the UI's render jobs: renders, makes a viewable mp4, prints "@@RESULT {json}")
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from . import motion
from .paths import PROJECTS, STUDIO

PREVIEWS = motion.MOTION / "previews"
RENDERS = PREVIEWS / "renders"          # viewable mp4 copies of UI render jobs
SIZES = {"landscape": (960, 540), "vertical": (540, 960)}
FPS = 30
TAIL_S = 0.5                            # transparent hold appended so hover loops breathe


def _run(cmd: list[str]) -> None:
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    if r.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"ffmpeg failed ({r.returncode}): {' '.join(cmd[:6])} ...\n{r.stderr[-2000:]}")


def _probe_duration(p: Path) -> float:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "csv=p=0", str(p)],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    try:
        return float(r.stdout.strip())
    except ValueError:
        return 0.0


def _game_sources() -> list[Path]:
    """Gameplay recordings referenced by projects, test-clip-02 first."""
    pjs = sorted(PROJECTS.glob("*/project.json"), key=lambda p: (p.parent.name != "test-clip-02", p.parent.name))
    out = []
    for pj in pjs:
        try:
            g = (json.loads(pj.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("sources") or {}).get("game", {}).get("file")
        except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            continue
        if g:
            f = Path(g) if Path(g).is_absolute() else pj.parent / g
            if f.exists() and f not in out:
                out.append(f)
    return out


def background(orientation: str = "landscape") -> Path:
    """Gameplay still (or checkerboard) sized for the orientation; extracted once and reused."""
    w, h = SIZES[orientation]
    out = PREVIEWS / f"_bg_{orientation}.jpg"
    if out.exists() and out.stat().st_size > 0:
        return out
    PREVIEWS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # cover-scale then centre-crop (vertical gets the middle of the landscape frame)
    vf = f"scale={w}:{h}:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop={w}:{h},setsar=1"
    for src in _game_sources():
        dur = _probe_duration(src)

70:- **title_card**: blocks rain in and stack into a plinth (0 to 0.9s). The title slams onto it at 0.95s with a screen shake and a burst of dust, the subtitle tag pops at 1.3s, and everything clears in the last 0.3s.
71:- **chapter**: an ink band with a gold under-stripe and stepped pixel edges wipes in from the left, the chapter name types in letter by letter, then the band wipes out to the right in the last 0.4s.
72:- **lower_third**: sits lower-left (landscape) or at 66% height (vertical, above the Shorts UI). It exits over the last 0.42s. `--duration` lengthens the hold.
73:- **subscribe**: a cursor clicks the stone button at 1.05s (it turns `accent` and reads SUBSCRIBED), then rings the bell at 1.86s. It exits at 3.2s.
74:- **counter**: the value ticks from 0.24s to 1.39s with a power2 in-out ease, then punches and flashes `accent`. Values are rounded integers.
75:- **hook_banner**: pops in at the top (8.5% from the top on vertical, clear of the Shorts header) and stays until the end with no exit. To keep it longer, use `--duration`, or let the renderer hold the last frame.
76:- **end_screen**: the video rectangles are left empty (transparent) and the borders sit outside them. In 1920x1080 output pixels: left video `x=100 y=360 w=760 h=428`, right video `x=1060 y=360 w=760 h=428`, subscribe circle `x=840 y=820 d=240`. The same rectangles are in `templates/end_screen/template.json` under `layout_1920x1080`. Place the YouTube end-screen elements on them. The vertical version stacks the frames.
77:- **mode_stinger**: the frame is **fully covered from 0.26s to 0.32s**, so cut the underlying footage at **0.29s** (`cut_at` in template.json). The label colour switches automatically between paper and ink for contrast.
80:More behaviour notes (newer templates):
81:- **pixel_wipe / block_break_wipe**: full-frame block transitions. Fully covered at 0.37-0.48s / 0.30-0.52s, so cut the footage at **0.42s** (`cut_at` in template.json). `style` picks the block texture.
82:- **countdown**: one second per number plus GO!. The duration follows `from` automatically (`from + 1`).
83:- **advancement_toast / hotbar_select / location_tag `icon`**: a built-in icon name, a data URI, a URL, or a local image path (motion.py inlines local files).
84:- **chat_message**: `lines` separated by `|`; `<Name> text` = player chat, otherwise yellow system text; `&a` colour codes work.
85:- **question_card**: side-by-side on landscape, stacked on vertical.

input.message:
All 6 Crodie templates are built in `studio/motion/templates/<name>/` (template.json, markup.html, template.css, template.js, plus generated landscape/ and vertical/). `npx hyperframes check` passes with 0 errors on all 12 projects. The only warnings are expected "path did not resolve" console warnings, because check uses the raw default paths; at render time motion.py inlines them. Preview renders are done for both orientations, sequentially. I composited mid-animation frames over gray and over the auto-dig gameplay frame and looked at them, and fixed what I saw. First and last frame alpha are 0 on every render. I ran one full 60fps spot-check (crodie_wipe, landscape). I did not touch motion.py, shared/ or any other template. In README I only inserted 6 table rows and 7 behaviour notes. I also generated UI previews (`motion/previews/crodie_*.mp4/.jpg/.json`) with `motion_previews`.

## Templates
Image vars default to studio-relative brand paths under `brand/crodie/...`. Every template also has `opaque` (false).

1. **crodie_wipe**: 1.0s transition. **`cut_at` 0.55**, `covered` [0.45, 0.65].
   - Measured full coverage (min alpha 255): 0.433–0.667s in the preview and 0.433–0.683s at 60fps.
   - Crodie dashes across with little hops and speed lines, followed by a wave of Crodie-skin tiles (lime/leaf/orange, 60px logical). The tiles pop out left to right by 0.96s.
   - Vars: `mascot` (characters/char_leap.png, "" = tiles only), `color` (brand grass), `direction` ("right" | "left" mirrors it).
   - For the EDL, start it 0.55s before the cut.
2. **crodie_verdict**: 1.8s. The badge stamps at 0.14s with a shake, flash and 3 shockwave rings. The emote pops at 0.36s at the badge's lower right.
   - `win`: rotating rays plus 44 brand-colour confetti pixels.
   - `lose`: grey pixel rain cloud, the badge droops, grey rings.
   - `neutral`: sparkles.
   - Vars: `badge` (emotes/badge_w.png), `emote` (emotes/fist_pump.png), `mood` ("win").
   - **The emote does not switch with mood.** The template can't load files itself, so for L pass `emote=brand/crodie/emotes/crying_waterfall.png` yourself.
3. **crodie_day_counter**: 2.5s. A grass-block plinth rises with "DAY" and the number on its face, and Crodie drops on and sits. The number ticks 0.5–1.6s, then punches to light orange while the crown drops onto the head with a glow, sparkles and bits.
   - Vars: `label` ("DAY"), `from` (1), `to` (47), `mascot` (characters/char_diamond_sitting.png), `crown` (logos/crown_1.png), `crown_x` (0.38), `position` ("center" | "left" | "right").
   - `crown_x` is the crown centre as a fraction of the mascot width, so it may need tuning for other mascots.
   - char_king_robe_scepter already wears a crown, so pass `crown=""` with it.
   - The final colour is a lighter orange because full brand orange failed the check's 3:1 contrast against the dirt.
4. **crodie_end_card**: 10s, stretchable to at least 5s. Dim olive/ink scrim, the logo_grass_main logo, two empty 16:9 slots in mossy pixel-wood frames with corner_vine.png, orange plank labels, an empty lime subscribe ring, and Crodie (char_jump_cheer) waving beside it.
   - Vars: `logo`, `mascot`, `vine`, `channel_name` (fallback when `logo` is ""), `left_label` ("WATCH NEXT"), `right_label` ("BEST VIDEO"), `sub_label` ("SUBSCRIBE"), `scrim` (0.6).
   - `layout_1920x1080` is identical to end_screen: video_left [100,360,760,428], video_right [1060,360,760,428], subscribe_circle [840,820,240,240].
   - I added `layout_1080x1920` for vertical: video_top [48,452,704,396], video_bottom [48,960,704,396], subscribe_circle [820,1060,200,200]. All of it sits inside the safe band.
   - I used CSS frames rather than overlays/frame_crown.png. That art is 1.32:1, so at 16:9 it would have to be stretched and the two frames would overlap.
   - **Unlike end_screen, it fades out over the last 0.3s** to meet your transparent-last-frame rule.
5. **crodie_thought**: 2.5s, stretchable to at least 1.6s. A Crodie head pops into the corner and a pixel bubble types the text letter by letter.
   - `thought` is a puffy stepped bubble with a trail of pixel dots; `speech` has a stepped wedge tail.
   - Text auto-fits up to 3 lines. The head bobs while speaking and tilts while thinking.
   - Vars: `text` ("wait... what?"), `kind` ("thought"), `position` ("bottom-left" | "bottom-right" | "top-left" | "top-right"), `head` (characters/char_head_smile.png).
6. **crodie_loot**: 2.2s. The emote pops in, then the item card spins up out of its hands (rotationY, 0.12–0.62s). After that come a flash, the rarity glow, rotating rays, sparkles, a rarity tag, the item name slamming in, and the count badge.
   - Vars: `item` ("DIAMONDS"), `count` ("3" shows as x3; a string, so literal text works; ""/0/1 = no badge), `rarity` ("rare"), `icon` ("" = built-in pixel diamond), `emote` (emotes/heart_eyes.png), `tag` ("auto" = rarity name, "" = none).
   - Rarity colours: common #F2F2F2, rare #4FA3FF, epic #B072FF, legendary #EF7718.
   - I added two vars you didn't ask for, `tag` and `crown_x`, and set `count` as a string.

## Worth knowing
- **Paths:** default image paths resolve through motion.py's studio-relative and channel-relative lookup, so they work from any cwd. An unresolved path or "" just skips that image.
- **Art sizing:** sizes are read from the PNG header and capped at about 0.9x native in logical px, which is about 1.8x native in full renders.
- **Vertical safe zones:** vertical layouts keep clear of the top ~10% and bottom ~26%.
- **Scratch tool:** the render-and-inspect script I used is `C:\Users\edmem\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-edmem-OneDrive-Desktop-Minecraft-Channel\ff88cddc-4e2b-4ed3-ae32-bc595258add8\scratchpad\crodie6\mt.py`, with frame PNGs in `out/`. It renders, composites over gray and gameplay, and prints alpha and coverage stats.
- **Scratchpad conflict:** someone left a `bisect.py` in the scratchpad root. It shadows Python's stdlib `bisect` for any script run from that folder, which is why my script lives in a subfolder.

## Worth knowing
- **Paths:** default image paths resolve through motion.py's studio-relative and channel-relative lookup, so they work from any cwd. An unresolved path or "" just skips that image.
- **Art sizing:** sizes are read from the PNG header and capped at about 0.9x native in logical px, which is about 1.8x native in full renders.
- **Vertical safe zones:** vertical layouts keep clear of the top ~10% and bottom ~26%.
- **Scratch tool:** the render-and-inspect script I used is `C:\Users\edmem\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-edmem-OneDrive-Desktop-Minecraft-Channel\ff88cddc-4e2b-4ed3-ae32-bc595258add8\scratchpad\crodie6\mt.py`, with frame PNGs in `out/`. It renders, composites over gray and gameplay, and prints alpha and coverage stats.
